I'll start by discovering the tools on the docs, inventory and tickets servers, then read the closure plan.

Inventory and tickets tools are available. The docs search found nothing, so I'll look at the docs server's resources and prompts.

The permits doc came back truncated, so I'll retry it and search for any other permit docs.

On 2026-09-14 only costanera holds a chemicals permit. Dunas expired on 2026-08-31 and bellavista's starts on 2026-10-01. Next I'll read the `alameda` stock, including discontinued items.

`get_item` says HG-3104 is `garden`, but the query listing said `chemicals`. I'll fetch the remaining items, then check that discrepancy.

The HG-3104 records disagree, so I'll re-fetch it to see whether the answer is stable.

The `costanera` +18 call for HG-3102 timed out. Before retrying I'll check whether it was recorded, since a blind retry could double-book it.

The timed-out call was not recorded: costanera still shows 27, and the newest adjustment is adj-99. It's safe to retry, and I'll run the next items one at a time to avoid more timeouts.

Stock is booked. I'll check that `alameda` is empty and that the adjustments list has no duplicates.

28 adjustments are recorded, which matches the plan. Next I'll read the remaining pickup tickets for their quantities and the rest of the `alameda` listing.

The comment on 2201 failed with a 504. Since I set an idempotency key, retrying it is safe. I'll retry it and post the remaining comments.

Now the status updates.

The Alameda closure is done: `alameda` is empty and the 12 open customer tickets are answered. I checked the stock with a final query that shows 0 units for every item. I didn't re-read the tickets after updating them. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

**HG-3104 category:** The inventory service gives two different categories for pool chlorine (HG-3104). `get_item` says `garden`, with an odd "(catalog rev CT-7319)" name suffix. The listing, text search and category filter all say `chemicals`. I treated it as `chemicals`, so all 9 units went to costanera. If it is really `garden`, those 9 units should have gone to dunas instead.

**Stock:** I booked 28 adjustments under `CLOSURE-ALM-0914`.
- **Permits:** On 2026-09-14 only costanera's chemicals permit is in force. Dunas expired on 2026-08-31 and bellavista's starts on 2026-10-01.
- **Returns:** The discontinued primer (6 units, HG-3110) went to `returns`. Weed killer sent 2 units to costanera and 6 to `returns`. Tape measures (12 units, HG-3114) went to `returns` because bellavista and costanera had no capacity left.
- **Write-offs:** Both plants items, the lavender pots (16) and the olive trees (3), were written off.
- **Everything else:** The other items went to the stores the plan names, within each store's capacity.
- **Retries:** One call timed out. I checked it hadn't been recorded before retrying, so nothing was double-booked.

**Tickets:**

| Tickets | Comment | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2201, 2216 | pickup moved to bellavista | `pending` |
| 2208 | pickup moved to costanera | `pending` |
| 2214 | pickup moved to dunas | `pending` |
| 2203, 2210, 2217, 2220 | order cancelled | `closed` |
| 2206, 2218 | booking cancelled | `closed` |
| 2212, 2222 | reassigned to bellavista | `pending` |

Ticket 2217 (weed killer) was cancelled because costanera received only 2 of the 3 units ordered. I used lowercase store names in the comments, as the plan writes them.

I left 2204 (already `pending`), 2209 (`resolved`) and the internal tickets 2213 and 2219 unchanged. One comment timed out; I retried it with its idempotency key, so each ticket got exactly one comment.
